note: A member's edge target must be a NAME. Two rules, both found by the lane's own second reader rather than by the shared differential (which does not audit `exports` at all for elixir): EX-EX11 routes `def unquote(x)` — a macro-GENERATED definition whose real name is computed at expansion time, and whose identifier `unquote` is reserved and can never be a member's name — to the documented EX-D9 placeholder, which the R7 guard keeps off every edge endpoint; the corpus case published `exports Date.Range -> unquote` for a callback that is really `member?/2`. EX-EX11b makes the placeholder guard case-SENSITIVE: the analyzer never writes a lowercase placeholder, and accepting one silently dropped the real public function `EExTest.Compiled.unknown/0` (eex_test.exs:29) from `contains` and `exports`. Both directions are pinned — `unquote` must not appear as an endpoint and `unknown` must — because a guard that rejected both would satisfy either assertion alone.

expectRelationships.note: EX-EX11b: a function genuinely named `unknown` is a public member; the lowercase spelling is not this analyzer's placeholder

forbidRelationships.note: EX-EX11: `unquote` is macro syntax, not a member name — the definition takes the EX-D9 placeholder and R7 keeps it off every edge endpoint
